user.title: Belgian Electricity Prices
user.description: Pick your supplier and region. Energy and grid rates are fetched live from the supplier's own publication.

contract.title: Contract
contract.description: Pick your contract. The integration fetches its current rate sheet on every refresh.

data_description.contract_start_date: The date your contract started. For a fixed contract this prices you at the rate you locked in at signing instead of today's rate sheet, where the supplier keeps an archive of past cards. Leave blank to always use the current card.
data_description.contract_end_date: The date your contract ends. Exposed as a timestamp sensor so an automation can remind you to renew, and used by the projected year cost to say how much of the year is still under this contract. It changes no billed rate.

signed_rate.title: Signing rate (optional)
signed_rate.description: Enter the rate you actually signed at. A promotional, brokered or negotiated rate appears on no published tariff card, so only you can supply it. What you type overrides the card box by box; leave a box blank to keep the card's value for it, or leave the whole step blank to price off the card alone. When your supplier archives past tariff cards, the card for your signing month fills the blanks; otherwise the current card does. Per-kWh values go in the same VAT basis your supplier prints on its card; the yearly fee goes in VAT-inclusive.

meter.title: Meter type
meter.description: Single-rate meter (mono), dual-time meter (peak/off-peak), or smart meter for dynamic contracts.

professional.title: Professional contract
professional.description: Professional tariff cards are published excluding VAT, and the federal excise is degressive by yearly volume. Two answers are needed to price them.

data_description.include_vat: Turn this off if your business deducts VAT: prices, fees and costs are then reported excluding it. Injection follows the same choice.
data_description.annual_consumption_kwh: Selects the excise band (bands at 20 000 and 50 000 kWh per year).

dso_tariff_mode.title: Distribution tariff (Wallonia)
dso_tariff_mode.description: How your DSO bills you for the network. 'Simple' / 'Bi-horaire' match the existing meter convention. 'Tarif Impact' uses the CWaPE 3-band hour-of-day rates (PIC 17-22, MEDIUM 7-11 + 22-1, ECO 1-7 + 11-17) and requires a smart meter.

connection_power.title: Connection power (Brussels)
connection_power.description: Your contractual connection power in kVA. Brussels bills a Brugel 'Obligations de Service Public' fee scaled by it. Residential connections are 13 kVA or less.

api_key.title: ENTSO-E API key
api_key.description: Required for dynamic contracts. Request one for free at transparency.entsoe.eu.

injection_api_key.title: ENTSO-E API key (injection)
injection_api_key.description: Optional. This contract indexes solar injection on the day-ahead spot, which needs a free ENTSO-E key from transparency.entsoe.eu. Leave blank to skip; without a key the injection price falls back to the figure printed on your tariff card, which is the previous month's, or stays unavailable if your card prints none.

capacity.title: Capacity tariff (Flanders)
capacity.description: Prefer your meter's own monthly peak sensor (DSMR 5B publishes "Maximum demand current month"), which is the quarter-hour peak Fluvius actually bills. A plain power sensor is sampled hourly and only approximates it. Or use a fixed value.

solar.title: Solar panels
solar.description: Inverter capacity in kVA and the regime that applies to your installation. The Walloon compensation regime is reserved for installations certified before 2024-01-01 and stays valid until 2030-12-31; new installations and Flemish smart meters are on the injection tariff.

meters.title: Energy meters (current year cost)
meters.description: Optional. Either point at the four day/night registers from your meter (preferred - exact from the start), or at single cumulative consumption / injection sensors (the integration reads kWh from HA's recorder and splits each past day's total into day/night via the bi-hourly schedule when needed). Each side - consumption, injection - is resolved independently; you can mix one side as registers and the other as a single total. When both wirings are filled for the same side, the day/night registers win. If you've already set up HA's Energy dashboard, the cumulative fields - and the day/night registers when a utility_meter helper splits the grid source into peak/offpeak (or jour/nuit, dag/nacht, piek/dal) tariffs - are pre-selected for you. Anything pre-filled stays editable.

data_description.day_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, will not work.
data_description.night_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, will not work.
data_description.day_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, will not work.
data_description.night_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, will not work.
data_description.consumption_kwh: Only used when the four registers above are empty: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.injection_kwh: Only used when the four registers above are empty: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.daily_compare: Off by default. Once a day, at a fixed time derived from this entry so installs do not all fetch at once, price every contract of your kind sold in your region and publish the yearly saving of the best one as a sensor. Most days this costs a handful of freshness checks, because tariff cards are republished about once a month.

custom_energy.title: Custom energy formula
custom_energy.description: Note: this is an expert option only for suppliers that publish NO public tariff card. If your supplier publishes one, please open a request to add it as a proper provider instead of using this: a hand-entered contract is a static snapshot with no live card refresh and no drift check, so the numbers only stay correct if you keep them up to date yourself. Enter your contract's commodity formula excluding VAT (as printed on your tariff sheet); the VAT rate on the taxes step grosses it up. For the dynamic and monthly-average modes the price is factor x index + base (index = the live spot, or the delivery month's mean spot). Example (Yuso dynamic): factor 1.0, base 0.02.

custom_injection.title: Custom injection formula
custom_injection.description: How your solar feed-in is paid. A flat rate is a fixed EUR/kWh credit; a formula is factor x index + base against the live spot (dynamic) or the monthly mean (monthly-average). Tick the floor if the contract guarantees the injection price is never negative. Tick 'weight injection by the solar profile' to weight the monthly injection mean by the Synergrid solar production profile (fetched live; an ex-ante forecast, so close to but not exactly the settled SPP value).

data.custom_injection_spp_weighted: Weight injection by the solar profile (SPP)

custom_dso.title: Grid (DSO) tariffs
custom_dso.description: Regulated grid costs, identical for every supplier on your DSO. Copy them from your bill or your DSO's tariff sheet, excluding VAT. Only distribution is required; leave anything you don't pay at 0.

custom_tax.title: Taxes and levies
custom_tax.description: Regulated taxes and levies, excluding VAT. The VAT rate below grosses up energy, grid and taxes (injection stays VAT-exempt). Belgian residential VAT is 0.06; set 0 if you entered VAT-inclusive numbers everywhere.

abort.already_configured: Another entry already polls the same (supplier, contract, region, DSO) combination. Edit that entry instead, or pick a different combination. An exclusive-night circuit is the exception: it is set up as its own additional entry, so it does not clash with your main one.

abort.compare_all_unknown_contract: This entry's contract is no longer in the supplier's catalogue, so it cannot be placed against the others. Re-pick it under Edit settings first.

edit.title: Belgian Electricity Prices
edit.description: Pick your supplier and region. Energy and grid rates are fetched live from the supplier's own publication.

compare.title: Compare another supplier
compare.description: Pick a supplier to quote against. Region, DSO and peak stay the same as your current entry; the meter type and the solar regime can be changed on a later step to quote a what-if. Both static and dynamic suppliers are listed, so you can quote across contract kinds.

compare_contract.title: Compare another supplier
compare_contract.description: Pick a contract from {supplier}. Both static and dynamic contracts are listed, so you can quote across contract kinds, and your own contract is listed too: pick it to ask what the same contract would cost with a different meter type or solar regime.

compare_meter.title: Compare another supplier
compare_meter.description: Meter type for the comparison. Defaults to your current entry's setting; change it to see what the bill would look like under a different billing mode (mono = single rate, bi = peak / off-peak).

compare_solar.title: Compare another supplier
compare_solar.description: Solar regime for this quote. Pick a different one to see what you would pay under another metering arrangement; the regime your entry uses is preselected. Unlike the meter type this applies to both sides, because the regime belongs to your grid connection and not to the supplier. Nothing is saved. The two volume fields appear when no injection meter is wired to this entry: a meter that runs backwards reports consumption already netted against injection, which is not what the injection tariff bills, so enter your gross yearly figures from your inverter app or your annual meter readout.

compare_api_key.title: Compare another supplier
compare_api_key.description: The option you picked needs ENTSO-E day-ahead spot prices to quote: a contract priced off the spot (a dynamic one per slot, a monthly-indexed one on the delivery month's mean), or a contract whose solar injection is priced off the hourly spot (Cociter Variable on the injection regime). Paste an ENTSO-E API token so the quote can fetch the spot prices. The token is used only for the quote and is not saved.

options.impact: Tarif Impact (3 bands by hour of day)

options.injection: Injection tariff (post-2024 install or smart meter)

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Force every Belgian Electricity Prices entry to re-fetch its supplier snapshot and today's ENTSO-E prices immediately, instead of waiting for the next refresh tick. This does not touch the cache of PAST hourly prices behind the year-to-date cost; use Clear price history for that.

clear_history.name: Clear price history
clear_history.description: Also discard the cached past hourly prices that the year-to-date cost replays, and re-fetch them. Off by default: it re-fetches every day since 1 January against a rate-limited endpoint. Use it when a year-to-date figure looks wrong in a way an ordinary refresh does not fix.

cheapest_window.name: Cheapest window
cheapest_window.description: Return the cheapest contiguous window of N hours in the upcoming price table.

duration_hours.name: Duration
duration_hours.description: Window length in whole hours. On a 15-minute contract the window may start on any quarter-hour boundary.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: Optional. Truncated down to the start of its price slot (the hour, or the quarter on a 15-minute contract), so 14:30 still considers the 14:00 slot. Defaults to now.

latest_end.name: Latest end
latest_end.description: Optional. Defaults to the end of the cached price table.

most_expensive_window.name: Most expensive window
most_expensive_window.description: Return the most expensive contiguous window of N hours in the upcoming price table.

duration_hours.name: Duration
duration_hours.description: Window length in whole hours. On a 15-minute contract the window may start on any quarter-hour boundary.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: Optional. Truncated down to the start of its price slot (the hour, or the quarter on a 15-minute contract), so 14:30 still considers the 14:00 slot. Defaults to now.

latest_end.name: Latest end
latest_end.description: Optional. Defaults to the end of the cached price table.

backfill_statistics.name: Backfill statistics
backfill_statistics.description: Populate the recorder's long-term statistics for this entry's price sensors and current_year_cost across a date range, so the Energy dashboard shows history that predates the entry's first live tick.

start.name: Start
start.description: First hour to backfill. Defaults to Jan 1 00:00 of the current local year.

end.name: End
end.description: First hour NOT to backfill (exclusive). Defaults to the current hour.

clear.name: Clear ENTIRE series before re-import
clear.description: Destructive: deletes every existing row of the target series (not just the requested range), then the re-import repopulates only the requested range. Use ONLY for a full-year re-run; a window that starts after Jan 1 of the end year is rejected with clear on, unless the window ends in a finished year (the cost series is left out of both the wipe and the re-import there). For narrower windows, leave this off: the import upserts on (statistic_id, hour) and already overwrites the requested hours without touching anything outside the range.

not_enough_hours.message: Only {available} price slots are available in the requested window; need {needed}.

no_loaded_entry.message: No loaded Belgian Electricity Prices entry.

no_loaded_entry_with_id.message: No loaded Belgian Electricity Prices entry with id {entry_id}.

entry_reloading.message: The entry is reloading; try again in a moment.

price_table_empty.message: The price table is empty; refresh the entry first.

snapshot_not_loaded.message: The supplier snapshot is not loaded yet; refresh the entry first.

snapshot_stale.title: Tariff data for {supplier} ({contract}) is more than {days} days old
snapshot_stale.description: The integration could not refresh the tariff card from the supplier and is serving cached data older than {days} days. Last fetch error: {last_error}. Prices may no longer reflect what is actually billed. Try the be_electricity_prices.refresh service, check your network, or open an issue on GitHub if the problem persists.

extractor_failed.title: Could not parse the tariff card for {supplier} ({contract})
extractor_failed.description: The supplier extractor raised an error: {error}. The integration is still serving the last successfully parsed prices, but they may no longer match what is actually billed. This usually means the supplier changed the layout of its tariff PDF or HTML page; please open an issue on GitHub with the supplier and contract so the extractor can be updated.

extractor_unreachable.title: Could not reach the supplier for {supplier} ({contract})
extractor_unreachable.description: The integration could not download the tariff card after several attempts: {error}. It is still serving the last successfully parsed prices. This is usually a temporary network or CDN problem that clears on the next refresh; run the be_electricity_prices.refresh service or check your network if it keeps happening.

extractor_unreadable.title: The tariff card for {supplier} can no longer be read
extractor_unreadable.description: {supplier} now publishes its tariff card as page images with no text layer, so the prices cannot be read from it. This one is not a bug in the integration and reporting it will not help: there is nothing in the document to read. This entry keeps serving the last prices it managed to parse ({contract}), and those drift further from your real bill every month the card is reissued. To stay accurate, either switch to another supplier, or add a Custom (expert) entry and type the values from your card in by hand. This card clears by itself if {supplier} goes back to publishing readable cards.

entsoe_auth_failed.title: ENTSO-E rejected the API key for {supplier} ({contract})
entsoe_auth_failed.description: transparency.entsoe.eu returned 401 for the configured API key: {error}. Edit the entry's options and replace the key with a fresh token from your transparency.entsoe.eu account (My Account Settings -> Web API Security Token). Until then this entry's dynamic price sensors will go unknown.

supplier_deprecated.title: {supplier} is transferring your contract to {successor} on {ends_on}
supplier_deprecated.description: {supplier} is leaving the residential energy market: your contract transfers automatically to {successor} on {ends_on}. Prices stay correct until {supplier} stops publishing its tariff card, so nothing is broken yet -- but this entry will stop updating afterwards. Edit the entry and select {successor} as the supplier once your transfer is confirmed.

supplier_deprecated_ended.title: {supplier} has transferred your contract to {successor}
supplier_deprecated_ended.description: {supplier} left the residential energy market on {ends_on} and your contract has transferred automatically to {successor}. It has stopped publishing a tariff card, so this entry can no longer update: it is still showing the last prices it read, and those are no longer what you are billed. Edit the entry and select {successor} as the supplier to start pricing your new contract.

supplier_deprecated_no_successor.title: {supplier} stops supplying residential energy on {ends_on}
supplier_deprecated_no_successor.description: {supplier} is leaving the residential energy market on {ends_on}. Prices stay correct until it stops publishing its tariff card, but this entry will stop updating afterwards. Your contract is being transferred to another supplier: check the letter they send you, then edit this entry and select that supplier. If it is not in the list, this integration does not cover it in your region yet -- please open an issue on GitHub.

supplier_deprecated_ended_no_successor.title: {supplier} has stopped supplying residential energy
supplier_deprecated_ended_no_successor.description: {supplier} left the residential energy market on {ends_on} and has stopped publishing a tariff card, so this entry can no longer update: it is still showing the last prices it read, and those are no longer what you are billed. Your contract has been transferred to another supplier: check the letter they sent you, then edit this entry and select that supplier. If it is not in the list, this integration does not cover it in your region yet -- please open an issue on GitHub.

exclusive_night_rate_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) does not publish an exclusive-night distribution rate
exclusive_night_rate_missing.description:
Your entry is configured for a separate exclusive-night meter circuit, but the tariff card {supplier} publishes for {dso} carries no exclusive-night distribution rate and no off-peak rate either. The integration is billing that circuit at the normal day distribution rate, so the network part of its price is higher than what you are actually charged. The energy part is unaffected.

Nothing can be substituted automatically: the integration never stores a price in its own source, and copying the figure from another supplier's card would be a guess. Ask {supplier} to print the exclusive-night distribution column, or switch this entry to a supplier whose card publishes it.

impact_rates_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) does not publish Tarif Impact rates for {dso}
impact_rates_missing.description:
This entry is set to the Wallonia Tarif Impact billing mode, but the tariff card {supplier} publishes for {contract} carries no PIC / MEDIUM / ECO distribution rates. The network part of the price falls back to the bi-hourly schedule while the energy part still follows the Impact bands, so the two disagree between 22:00 and 01:00, where Impact bills MEDIUM.

The bill stays close, but you are not being billed on the tariff you opted into. Switch this entry's DSO billing mode to bi-hourly, or pick a contract whose card publishes the Impact block.

connection_fee_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) no longer publishes the Walloon connection fee
connection_fee_missing.description:
Since the August 2026 card, {supplier} has stopped printing the "Redevance de raccordement" row on its Walloon tariff cards. Wallonia still levies this charge and the card's own terms keep taxes and network fees fully passed through, but the rate is published nowhere this integration can read.

Prices for this entry therefore exclude it, which under-bills by roughly 0,075 c€/kWh (about €2.60 per year at 3500 kWh). Everything else on the card, including the new flat federal excise, is priced normally. This notice clears automatically once {supplier} prints the row again.
